text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- The State Ownership Fund would speed up the privatisation process, said Valentin Ionescu, head of the National Privatisation Agency.
- The central bank (BNR) is to adopt the rules for portfolio investments.
- The newspaper publishes a list of credits worth $1.1 billion granted to Romania by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) for 30 projects.
ADEVARUL
- The four percent cut in wage taxes proposed by the government is an insult to millions of employees, says the newspaper.
- One million hectare of 2.4 million under wheat has yet to be harvested, says the newspaper.
- The central bank (BNR) will closely watch the private Columna Bank after 10 leading bank officials were dismissed by a BNR decision.
- Losses caused by heavy rains over the past weeks are estimated at some 800 billion lei.

- The economi crime fighting unit is investigating the former chief and other officials of the leading state-run Bancorex bank over alleged illegal credits granted in 1992 causing losses worth 3.99 trillion lei and $137.4 million.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Wages will rise 17 percent starting July and another six percent in the fourth quarter of 1997.
- The State Ownership Fund will allocate Navrom and Romline, two major shipping companies, almost $14 million to release ships detained across the world.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper presents latest data on land under wheat, corn, sunflowers, sugar beet, potatoes, vegetables as well as vineyards damaged by rains.
General:
ADEVARUL
- Justice Minister Valeriu Stoica is under investigation over an alleged forgery of adoption documents for two girls.
- Gigolos and strip tease shows with men are common for the billionare women in Romania, says the newspaper in a full-page report.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Former President Ion Iliescu said this winter or the latest next year there will be early general elections.

- Eighteen Greek Catholics, including a priest, barricaded themselves inside the sole church in a village in northern Romania to protest against a court decision banning them from sharing the church with Orthodox congregations for masses.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper publishes the advertising draft bill.
- Over 1,150 tonnes of unidentified toxic waste lies around Romania, says the newspaper.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
